title.narrative: Activity under preparation DREAM Kenya ¿ Democratic Resilience and Electoral Accountability to Meet Popular Demands in Kenya¿s 2027 electoral cycle

description.narrative: Contract related to: DREAM Kenya ¿ Democratic Resilience and Electoral Accountability to Meet Popular Demands in Kenya¿s 2027 electoral cycle - Upholding democratic governance goes far beyond single electoral events and requires informed citizen engagement through credible, transparent and inclusive decision-making processes that enhance the effectiveness, responsiveness and legitimacy of public policies. This action will reaffirm the EU¿s position as a reliable partner in supporting African ownership in the implementation of the African Union Transitional Justice Policy (AUTJP) ; provide comprehensive electoral support at national, regional and continental levels; and enhance accountability mechanisms integrating a human rights-based approach (HRBA) perspective, including oversight by independent media, open governance reforms, and the fight against tax evasion, fraud, and illicit financial flows to reinforce credible inclusive democratic institutions, sustain resilient and accountable democracies, and increase tax transparency and domestic resource mobilisation. In a context of an evolving autocratic wave[1] and increasing political instability affecting in particular Sub-Saharan Africa, the action aligns with EU and AU strategies and interests, including that of promoting a rules-based order, enhancing the respect for human rights and gender equality and ultimately fulfilling African citizens¿ aspirations for a democracy that delivers positive outcomes.[2] The proposed action adopts a multi-level, multi-stakeholder approach, recognising that sustainable solutions require coordination across continental, regional, and national levels. It aims to strengthen African institutions, enhance electoral integrity, promote independent media and accountable governance, ultimately contributing to a more stable and prosperous continent.Transitional Justice (TJ) is considered at the highest political level by the African Union (AU) as a tool for conflict prevention and resolution, essential for addressing the root causes of conflict and building the foundation for lasting peace and sustainable development. Operationalising ¿African solutions to African problems¿, AU Member States (MS) have demanded increased support from the AU to implement the AUTJP and its roadmap. Hence, building on a predecessor project[3] under AAP 2022, greater emphasis will be placed on capacitating AU MS and regional bodies such as ECOWAS, SADC, IGAD and ECCAS.To enhance electoral processes, SO2 (Electoral Support) will extend beyond traditional technical and logistical support to election management bodies and State institutions, incorporating support for civil society, voter education, and independent media to ensure fair democratic coverage. The EU will promote a coherent approach by supporting the implementation of EU Election Observation Missions¿ (EU EOMs) recommendations and harmonising pan-African electoral capacities. To counter shrinking civic space, the action will strengthen regional CSO networks for election observation and foster structured collaboration between the AU, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and corresponding CSO platforms.The action will also promote accountability by strengthening independent media, advancing open governance reforms, and reinforcing the fight against tax fraud, evasion, and illicit financial flows. Support to media will focus on strengthening the resilience and financial sustainability of independent media and investigative journalism.
